content.title: Toyota: 550,000 Highlander 2021 to 2024 model vehicles recalled over recliner defect
content.text: Skip to content by: Rob Taub Posted: Mar 12, 2026 / 07:12 AM EDT Updated: Mar 12, 2026 / 07:12 AM EDT SHARE (NewsNation) — Toyota announced earlier this week that it has recalled 550,000 Highlander model vehicles over a recliner defect. The recall affects certain model year 2021-2024 Highlander and Highlander Hybrid vehicles, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. “The recliner assemblies in the second-row seats may not fully lock after seat back adjustment,” Toyota said in a news release. “A seat back that has not been secured in a locked position may fail to properly restrain occupants, increasing the risk of injury in the event of a crash at higher speeds.” $7.25B settlement over Roundup weed killers: Who qualifies, and how much you could receive Toyota says dealers will resolve the issue by replacing the return springs in the seat back recliner assemblies, free of charge. The car manufacturer said owners of the models will also receive a letter notifying them of the safety risk next month.
